result.title: Depth-Linked Residual Tokens for Multimodal Retrieval and Generation
result.summary: Iterative architectures such as looped language models improve parameter efficiency and reasoning capacity of transformers, yet their sequential backbone iterations introduce substantial computational latency. Conversely, parallelizable learnable special tokens (such as the register tokens in Vision Transformer) enable efficient single-pass inference, but often suffer from the absence of sequential refinement and exhibit redundant representations across tokens. To address these challenges, we introduce Depth-Linked Residual Tokens (DepThink), an efficient framework designed for multimodal retrieval and generation. Operating within a single pre-filling forward pass, DepThink appends a sequence of K learnable residual tokens whose hidden states are coupled through a lightweight, learnable residual recurrence. This mechanism enables each residual token to progressively capture complementary information missed by preceding tokens. Theoretically, we prove that DepThink provides strictly expanded geometric directional reachability over standard learnable tokens and guarantees a provable one-step descent advantage. We evaluate DepThink across multimodal retrieval and generation tasks. DepThink consistently outperforms learnable-token baselines and matches or exceeds looped architectures across dense (2B, 8B) and sparse mixture-of-experts (30B-A3B) backbones under both LoRA and full-parameter fine-tuning, while accelerating training by up to 11.9 and inference by 4.3 over looped architectures.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 DepThink：在单次 pre-filling 前向中追加 K 个可学习 residual token，用轻量可学习残差递推耦合其隐藏状态，使后序 token 逐步捕获前序遗漏的信息，并给出方向可达性与一步下降的理论分析；在多模态检索与生成上优于可学习 token 基线、匹配或超过 looped 架构，同时加速训练与推理。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接触及以并行 latent token 替代串行循环的状态生成问题，且明确针对 token 间表示冗余与互补信息缺失，可作为核查多 latent 假设的表达多样性、信息坍缩及计算—收益权衡的线索，但其 residual token 是否真正承载视觉证据并影响答案仍需读原文。
